# vangle

> Reactive documents for static HTML, after Bret Victor's Tangle, with KaTeX support. Authors write custom elements (`<t-num>`, `<t-out>`, `<t-math>`, …) in plain HTML or Markdown, and readers drag numbers in the text or inside formulas while everything that depends on them updates.

- It is one ES module (`tangle.js`) and one stylesheet (`tangle.css`), with no build step and no dependencies. Add `<link rel="stylesheet" href="tangle.css">` and `<script type="module" src="tangle.js"></script>` to the page.
- To load it from a CDN instead, use jsDelivr: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/koaning/vangle@v0.1.0/tangle.min.css">` and `<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/koaning/vangle@v0.1.0/tangle.min.js"></script>`. A module that imports from `tangle.js` must use the same URL as the `<script>` tag, or it gets a second copy with separate variables.
- Variables are declared by elements, and declaration order doesn't matter. Expressions are plain JavaScript over those variables, plus `Math` and a few other globals.
- Without JavaScript, every element shows its fallback text, so feeds and readers stay readable.
- Each docs page below is Markdown with live examples written as raw HTML blocks. Those blocks are exactly the markup to copy.

## Docs

- [Getting started](docs/index.md): install, a first reactive paragraph, and how variables, reactivity and scopes work. Keywords: basics, first paragraph, declare, reactive.
- [Expressions & formats](docs/expressions.md): what names an expression can use, registering functions, conditional text, and printf-style and named formats. Keywords: format, %.2f, if, ternary.
- [Updating a chart](docs/charts.md): for charts `<t-vega>` and `<t-obsplot>` don't cover: drawing an SVG chart with fixed scales from the variables with `scopeOf(...).effect`, canvas and chart libraries, and setting variables from a click in the chart. Keywords: custom plot, d3, canvas.
- [Your own elements](docs/custom-elements.md): writing custom elements by extending `TangleElement`: `watch` effects that stop on disconnect, `declare` from attributes, and `makeDraggable` for a widget that drags like `<t-num>`. Examples: a bar, a range slider, a row of draggable dots. Keywords: custom widget, range slider, dots.
- [Using it on a blog](docs/blogging.md): layouts, raw-HTML settings for Markdown generators, KaTeX setup, CSP and feeds. Keywords: static site, publish.

## Elements

- [`<t-num>`](docs/t-num.md): a number the reader can drag, type or step with the keyboard. Keywords: slider, scrubber, parameter, input.
- [`<t-var>`](docs/t-var.md): declares a variable without showing it, for example a formula parameter. Keywords: constant, parameter, state.
- [`<t-let>`](docs/t-let.md): a named value computed from other variables. Keywords: derived, formula, compute.
- [`<t-out>`](docs/t-out.md): shows the live result of an expression in the text. Keywords: display, print, value.
- [`<t-choice>`](docs/t-choice.md): a word the reader clicks to cycle through options, or a toggle. Keywords: options, boolean, switch.
- [`<t-select>`](docs/t-select.md): a word the reader clicks to pick from a searchable menu of options, for lists too long to cycle through. Same `options` as `<t-choice>`; set `el.options` from JavaScript for generated lists. Keywords: menu, long list, pick.
- [`<t-text>`](docs/t-text.md): a piece of text the reader clicks to rewrite; its variable holds a string. Keywords: text input, label, name.
- [`<t-call>`](docs/t-call.md): shows `<t-num>`, `<t-choice>` and `<t-text>` children as the arguments of a function call, `fn(a=1, b='x')`, with the return value as a variable. `tangleCall(fn, options)` builds one from a JavaScript function's parameter defaults. Keywords: arguments, signature.
- [`<t-fetch>`](docs/t-fetch.md): a variable whose value comes from a server. `url` is a template with `${…}` expressions, `params` an expression for the query string and `body` one for a JSON POST body; it requests again when the variables they read change, with a debounce, and only the newest answer lands. While it waits, the old value stays and elements that depend on it get the class `is-stale` (dimmed). `loading` and `error` name variables for the state. Answers are cached for the page; `cache="local"` also keeps them in `localStorage`, revalidating on load. Keywords: api, http, json, server, data.
- [`<t-codecell>`](docs/t-codecell.md): JavaScript the reader edits (CodeMirror, loaded lazily), run in a Web Worker, with its result in the variable `name`. The code is the element's text, or in a `<script type="text/plain">` when it has `<` or `&`: one expression, or statements with `return`; `await` works. Page variables it mentions are passed in by value and it reruns when they or the code change; the old result stays, dimmed, while it runs. Below the editor: `console.log` lines and errors with line numbers, plus the value with `output` (or when there is no `name`). `timeout` (ms, default 2000) stops endless loops; `copy` adds a Copy button; `registerEngine(lang, factory)` adds other languages. Keywords: code editor, repl, sandbox.
- [`<t-tag>`](docs/t-tag.md): shows an HTML tag, `<input type="range" max="10">`, whose attributes are `<t-num>`, `<t-choice>` and `<t-text>` children, with the live element rendered below it. Useful for documenting an element's attributes. Keywords: attributes, documentation.
- [`<t-math>`](docs/t-math.md): a KaTeX formula with draggable `\tangle{}` parameters and live `\val{}` results. Keywords: equation, latex, tex.
- [`<t-formula-dag>`](docs/t-formula-dag.md): formulas that build on each other, drawn as a DAG. The spec is a JavaScript object in a `<script type="text/plain">`, with TeX in `String.raw` strings. `\use{name}` puts another formula's symbol in and draws an arrow to that spot. Formulas sit one row below the deepest formula they use; `row: n` pushes one down to at least row n. A formula's `value` (an expression or a function) defines a variable of its name. `\tangle{}` numbers, `\note{name}{tex}` notes with their text in `notes`, a legend of chips, Reset, and `name="x"` for the clicked formula. Keywords: derivation, dependencies, model.
- [`<t-vega>`](docs/t-vega.md): a Vega-Lite chart (JSON spec in a `<script type="application/json">`, or `src`). Spec params and named data sources with a variable's name are linked to it; Vega loads from jsDelivr only on pages that use it. Keywords: chart, json spec, plot.
- [`<t-obsplot>`](docs/t-obsplot.md): an Observable Plot chart, written as a JavaScript expression (Plot options or an array of marks) in a `<script type="text/plain">`, or `src`. It can use `Plot`, `d3` and the variables, and redraws when a variable it read changes. `name="x"` puts the datum under Plot's pointer into `x`. d3 and Plot load from jsDelivr only on pages that use it. Keywords: chart, line, scatter, histogram.
- [`<t-jsxgraph>`](docs/t-jsxgraph.md): a JSXGraph board of points, lines and curves, built by a script in a `<script type="text/plain">` (or `src`) that runs once with `board`, `JXG` and `point(x, y)` in reach. Functions on the board can read variables, and `point("x", "y")` makes a draggable point that sets two variables (snapped to their min, max and step) and follows them. Colors come from CSS. JSXGraph loads from jsDelivr only on pages that use it. Keywords: geometry, curves, construction.
- [`<t-graph>`](docs/t-graph.md): a force-directed graph (d3-force, loaded lazily from jsDelivr). The spec is a JavaScript expression in a `<script type="text/plain">` (or `src`), with `d3` in reach, giving `{ nodes, edges, directed }`; it reruns when a variable it read changes. The attributes `height` (400), `distance` (60, edge length) and `charge` (-160, repulsion) set how it's drawn. Nodes are strings, numbers or `{ id, name, size, color, data, x, y }`; edges are `[source, target]` pairs or `{ source, target, name, width, color, data }`, with endpoints by id, unique name or index. A color is CSS, `"light dark"`, or a number 1–8 from the theme palette. Nodes that keep their id keep their position, and new ones start next to a neighbour. `name="x"` holds the clicked node object (two-way: setting an id picks it), `hover="h"` the node under the pointer; both null when there's none. The layout is free and the view scales it down to fit the box (never up); `bounded` instead clamps nodes inside the box at full size. With the `zoom` attribute, Ctrl/Cmd + wheel or a pinch zooms (1–8×), dragging the background pans, and a Reset zoom button appears; a plain wheel still scrolls the page. Keywords: network, tree, d3-force.
- [`<t-paint>`](docs/t-paint.md): a canvas the reader draws on, with brush, marker, eraser, color picker, undo and clear. With `name`, the drawing is a variable holding a PNG data URL, updated when a stroke ends; setting the variable loads a picture. The element's `canvas` property gives the pixels. Keywords: sketch, brush, image.
- [`<t-sketch>`](docs/t-sketch.md): an infinite whiteboard of vector strokes, the board of Sketcher without its LaTeX layer: pen, marker (overlapping highlights of one color stay even), stroke eraser and lasso select (move, resize, delete, copy/paste between boards), with undo/redo, plain/dots/grid paper, and a right-click menu (zoom to fit, export or copy a PNG, clear). Shift draws a straight line at 15° steps and Option/Alt snaps it to the grid. Ctrl/⌘ + scroll or a pinch zooms (0.1–8×); a plain scroll pans only once the board has focus; Space-drag and two fingers pan. Its children are cards placed with `data-x`, `data-y`, `data-width` (280) in board coordinates, under the ink, so you draw arrows between live widgets; the select tool moves them. `mode="edit"` (default) has Preview (the board as readers see it, cards live, drag pans) and Export, which copies the HTML of a `mode="view"` copy: the cards' original HTML at their new places plus the ink in an inline `<script type="application/json">` (`exportHTML()` returns it). View mode only pans and zooms. Both modes have a full-screen button. Attributes `height` (400), `background` (dots), `src` (a JSON file of a board) and `label`. With `name`, the variable holds the board as JSON (Sketcher's format) `{ background, math, strokes: [{ id, tool, color, swatch, width, points: [[x, y], …] }], version: 2 }`, set when a stroke or edit ends; setting it (an object or JSON text) shows that board. `toPNG()` gives a cropped PNG data URL, and a `change` event fires on each edit. Palette colors follow the page's light or dark theme. Keywords: whiteboard, infinite canvas, vector drawing, sketcher.
- [`<t-scope>`](docs/t-scope.md): gives part of the page its own set of variables. Keywords: isolate, namespace.
- [`<t-debug>`](docs/t-debug.md): the variables as a live dependency graph (SVG, values left, each formula right of what it reads), for debugging while writing, with a table below listing each one's kind (value, formula with its run count, fetch, or never set), value or error, the variables it reads and is read by, and the elements that show it. Inside a `<t-scope>` it shows that scope, elsewhere every scope. `?tangle-debug` in a page's URL floats one over the page. `inspectScope(scope)` returns the same rows as data, for scripts and agents, and `layoutGraph(rows)` the positions of the graph. Keywords: inspect, debugging.
- [`<t-panel>`](docs/t-panel.md): floats its contents (typically controls) in a draggable, minimizable panel fixed to a corner of the viewport. The children keep their scope. Keywords: sidebar, sticky, controls.

## Gallery

Complete small documents that combine the elements with a script.

- [Matrix transformations](docs/gallery-matrix.md): a 2×2 matrix in `<t-math>` whose entries are draggable, drawn as a warped plane. Dragging the basis arrows sets the variables, and preset buttons animate between matrices. Keywords: linear algebra, svg, animation.
- [Amdahl's law](docs/gallery-amdahl.md): speedup against cores for two programs with draggable serial fractions, built from markup alone: a list of `<t-num>`s and `<t-out>`s, a `<t-let>` per program and a `<t-obsplot>` chart. Keywords: t-let, t-obsplot, no script.
- [The winner's curse](docs/gallery-winners-curse.md): simulated auctions where the highest guess overpays. Sections share page-wide variables, a script registers seeded random functions for the expressions, and `<t-obsplot>` charts show one auction, thousands of auctions (the count is draggable), up to 100 bidders, and the cure of shaving your bid. Keywords: simulation, seeded random, registerFunction.

- [Throwing darts at a drawing](docs/gallery-darts.md): a Monte Carlo estimate of the area of a shape the reader paints in `<t-paint>`. Registered functions read the canvas's pixels, a `<t-obsplot>` shows the darts over the drawing (`Plot.image` of the data URL) and how the estimate settles, and the starting disc gives an estimate of π. Keywords: t-paint, pixels, estimate pi.
- [A Gaussian mixture, drawn as a DAG](docs/gallery-mixture.md): two bell curves and a weight, with `<t-num>`s for μ₁, σ₁, μ₂, σ₂ and w and `<t-obsplot>`s for each group and the mixture, all as cards on a view-mode `<t-sketch>` with the dependency arrows drawn in ink. The board was arranged and drawn in edit mode and pasted from its Export. Keywords: mixture model, t-sketch cards, hand-drawn DAG.
- [What recomputes](docs/gallery-recompute.md): two `<t-let>`s and a registered `count` function that bumps a counter variable each time a variable runs, showing that only dependents re-run and that a variable read in several places runs once. Keywords: reactivity, performance.
- [Bézier curves](docs/gallery-bezier.md): de Casteljau's construction of a cubic Bézier curve in `<t-jsxgraph>`. Four draggable JSXGraph control points, mixed points that read a `<t-var>` `t` inside functions, the curve drawn up to `t`, a `<t-math>` formula whose weights are live `\val{}`s, and a Play button that animates `t`. Keywords: animation, t-jsxgraph.
- [Coaster nausea](docs/gallery-coaster-nausea.md): intensity against nausea for 142 RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 coasters, loaded by a `<t-fetch>` that sends a SQL query to datasette. A `<t-choice>` keeps, fixes or drops a broken row (the correlation goes from 0.20 to 0.72), and a `<t-math>` fit with a draggable intensity shows how far real rides spread around the line. Keywords: data, outliers.
- [Attention](docs/gallery-attention.md): one self-attention layer with two-number embeddings, as an SVG flow diagram in the order it runs (projections, QKᵀ, scale, mask, softmax, AV). The diagram is data: nodes with the step they run in, and edges labelled with matrix shapes. A `<t-num>` step, Back/Next/Play buttons and clicks on nodes walk through it, with a panel of heatmaps for each step. Draggable W_Q, W_K and W_V in `<t-math>`, page-wide variables shared with two SVG planes where dragging a token sets its embedding, and `<t-choice>`s for the causal mask and the query token. Keywords: transformer, heatmap, stepper.
- [McNugget numbers](docs/gallery-mcnugget.md): which counts of nuggets boxes of 6, 9 and 20 can make, as a `<t-graph>` tree from 0 where each count joins the one it extends by a box, along the fewest boxes. `<t-num>`s for the box sizes and the limit, `<t-let>` tables for the fewest boxes and the gaps, `hover` to spell out a count's boxes, and the largest count that can't be bought (43, the Frobenius number). Keywords: number theory, hover.
- [Projectile motion with wind](docs/gallery-projectile.md): nine formulas in a `<t-formula-dag>`, from launch speed, angle, gravity and a constant wind push to where the ball lands. Each formula has a `value`, so `<t-out>`s and two `<t-obsplot>` charts (side view and from above) read the results straight from the diagram. Notes, a long arrow that skips rows, and `<t-num>`s in the text that share variables with the formulas. Keywords: physics, values.

## Reference

- [JavaScript API](docs/javascript.md): `scopeOf`, scope methods, effects, `TangleElement`, signals, `registerFunction`, `registerFormat`, `tangleCall` and `configure`. Keywords: script, module.
- [Styling](docs/styling.md): CSS custom properties, selectors and states, recipes and dark mode. Keywords: theme, colors, css.
